evaluations.bottleneck: Before Transformer architecture, training sequence models on long contexts was impossible or impractical because recurrent networks processed tokens sequentially and could not be parallelized.

Q1.evidence: The Transformer reached state-of-the-art translation quality while training for only 3.5 days on eight GPUs, a regime recurrent models could not match at that quality.
Q1.falsification: this pass dies if recurrent models of 2017 are shown to have matched Transformer quality and training cost at scale

Q10.evidence: By 2020 Transformers had displaced LSTMs as the default architecture for state-of-the-art NLP.
Q10.falsification: this pass dies if LSTMs remained the default for leading NLP systems after 2020

Q11.evidence: The GPT lineage that powers modern agents descends directly from the 2017 Transformer paper.
Q11.falsification: this pass dies if the GPT lineage is shown to derive from a different architecture

Q12.evidence: No major lab has returned to recurrent architectures as the default for frontier language models since Transformers scaled.
Q12.falsification: this pass dies if frontier language modeling reverts to RNN defaults

Q2.evidence: Transformers became the substrate for BERT, GPT, ViT and multimodal models, unblocking a whole family of previously impractical systems.
Q2.falsification: this pass dies if post-2017 large models are shown to rest mainly on non-Transformer architectures
Q2.source: Attention Is All You Need

Q3.evidence: Every major LLM core behind 2023 agents, including GPT-4 class systems, is a Transformer variant.
Q3.falsification: this pass dies if a 2023-class agent is shown to have emerged on a non-Transformer core at comparable capability

Q4.evidence: Removing recurrence allowed full parallelization across sequence positions, sharply cutting training time per experiment compared with sequential RNN training.
Q4.falsification: this pass dies if Transformer training is shown to have been no faster than comparable RNN training

Q6.evidence: Self-attention gave designers an explicit model of sequence processing as learned pairwise token interaction, enabling deliberate variants such as encoder-only and decoder-only models.
Q6.falsification: this pass dies if Transformer variants are shown to have been designed without using the attention interaction model

Q7.evidence: The Transformer block became a reusable standard component implemented identically across frameworks and model families.
Q7.falsification: this pass dies if later models are shown not to reuse a common Transformer block abstraction
Q7.source: Attention Is All You Need

Q8.evidence: The same architecture produced leading results in language, vision, speech and protein structure prediction.
Q8.falsification: this pass dies if Transformers are shown to have remained confined to machine translation

Q9.evidence: Parallel training shortened the train-evaluate cycle from sequential RNN runs to highly parallel GPU and TPU runs, enabling rapid scaling experiments.
Q9.falsification: this pass dies if Transformer iteration cycles are shown to have been as slow as RNN cycles at equal scale

evaluations.bottleneck: Before self-attention mechanism, relating distant tokens in a sequence was impossible or impractical because recurrence passed information step by step through a sequential bottleneck.

Q1.evidence: Self-attention connects all positions with a constant number of sequential operations, making direct long-range dependency modeling practical.
Q1.falsification: this pass dies if recurrent paths are shown to have offered equally direct long-range access at scale

Q10.evidence: Attention-based mixing replaced recurrence as the default sequence mixing operation in NLP after 2017.
Q10.falsification: this pass dies if recurrence remained the default sequence mixer in leading NLP after 2019

Q11.evidence: Self-attention is the defining operation in the direct ancestry of every GPT model.
Q11.falsification: this pass dies if GPT models are shown not to use self-attention

Q12.evidence: Successor architectures still retain attention or explicitly position themselves against it, showing the field reorganized permanently around it.
Q12.falsification: this pass dies if attention disappears from both practice and successor design debates

Q2.evidence: Self-attention underlies language models, vision transformers and multimodal encoders, opening many model classes beyond translation.
Q2.falsification: this pass dies if self-attention is shown to have been used only inside the original translation model
Q2.source: Attention Is All You Need

Q3.evidence: All Transformer LLM cores used by modern agents implement self-attention as their core mixing operation.
Q3.falsification: this pass dies if agent LLM cores are shown to work at scale without any attention-like token mixing

Q6.evidence: Attention weights provide an explicit pairwise relevance model that researchers used to design heads, masking and sparse variants.
Q6.falsification: this pass dies if head and masking design are shown to owe nothing to the pairwise relevance model

Q7.evidence: Multi-head attention became a standard module exported by every major deep learning framework.
Q7.falsification: this pass dies if multi-head attention is shown not to be a reusable framework module
Q7.source: Attention Is All You Need

Q8.evidence: Self-attention was transferred from text to images in ViT and to proteins in AlphaFold-style architectures.
Q8.falsification: this pass dies if self-attention is shown to have no successful use outside text

evaluations.bottleneck: Before attention mechanism (neural machine translation), neural translation was impossible or impractical for long sentences because the source had to be compressed into one fixed-length vector.

Q11.evidence: Transformer self-attention directly generalizes the 2014 alignment mechanism by removing the recurrent decoder it was attached to.
Q11.falsification: this pass dies if Transformer attention is shown to have an independent origin unrelated to NMT attention
Q11.source: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate

Q6.evidence: Bahdanau attention introduced learned soft alignment as an explicit model of which source words a decoder step should use.
Q6.falsification: this pass dies if the 2014 model is shown not to learn source-target alignments
Q6.source: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate

evaluations.bottleneck: Before sequence-to-sequence learning, mapping inputs to outputs of different lengths was impossible or impractical in one trainable model because tasks needed bespoke architectures per input-output shape.

Q11.evidence: Prompt-to-response language modeling is a direct descendant of the seq2seq framing of conditional sequence generation.
Q11.falsification: this pass dies if conditional generation in LLMs is shown to have a separate, unrelated origin
Q11.source: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks

Q2.evidence: Seq2seq was applied to translation, summarization, parsing and speech, showing one framework covered many transduction tasks.

Q6.evidence: The encoder-decoder framework gave a general explanatory template of compressing an input sequence then generating an output sequence.
Q6.falsification: this pass dies if later sequence models are shown not to use or react against the encoder-decoder template
Q6.source: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks

Q7.evidence: Encoder-decoder became a standard interface reused in translation, summarization and later Transformer models such as T5.
Q7.falsification: this pass dies if encoder-decoder structure is shown not to recur across later systems
Q7.source: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks

Q8.evidence: Seq2seq methods spread from translation into speech recognition, dialogue and code generation.

evaluations.bottleneck: Before long short-term memory (LSTM), learning long-range dependencies was impossible or impractical because vanilla recurrent gradients vanished or exploded over long time lags.

Q1.evidence: LSTM constant-error carousels learned tasks with lags of over 1000 steps that vanilla RNNs could not learn.
Q1.falsification: this pass dies if vanilla RNNs of 1997 are shown to learn 1000-step lag tasks equally well

evaluations.bottleneck: Before backpropagation popularized, training multi-layer networks was impossible or impractical because there was no demonstrated general method for assigning credit to hidden units.

Q1.evidence: Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams showed backpropagation trained multi-layer networks to learn useful internal representations on tasks earlier perceptrons could not solve.
Q1.falsification: this pass dies if multi-layer networks are shown to have been routinely trained effectively before 1986 by another general method

Q10.evidence: Gradient-trained neural networks displaced hand-engineered feature pipelines as the default in perception and language by the 2010s.
Q10.falsification: this pass dies if hand-engineered pipelines remained the default in perception and language after 2015

Q11.evidence: Backpropagation is in the direct training lineage of AlexNet, Transformers and GPT models.
Q11.falsification: this pass dies if those systems are shown to use a different training principle

Q12.evidence: No subsequent paradigm has replaced gradient backpropagation as the training method for frontier neural networks.
Q12.falsification: this pass dies if frontier networks abandon backpropagation as their training method

Q2.evidence: Backpropagation underlies training of convolutional, recurrent and Transformer networks across virtually all of deep learning.
Q2.falsification: this pass dies if major deep learning systems are shown to train without gradient backpropagation
Q2.source: Learning representations by back-propagating errors (Nature)

Q3.evidence: Every LLM core behind modern agents is trained by backpropagating loss gradients through the network.
Q3.falsification: this pass dies if an LLM-class model is shown trained to comparable capability without backpropagation

Q6.evidence: Backpropagation supplied the credit-assignment model that let researchers deliberately design and debug layered architectures.
Q6.falsification: this pass dies if architecture design after 1986 is shown to owe nothing to gradient credit assignment

Q7.evidence: Automatic differentiation of a scalar loss, built on backpropagation, is the standard training interface in PyTorch and TensorFlow.
Q7.falsification: this pass dies if modern frameworks are shown not to expose backpropagation-based training as their core interface
Q7.source: Learning representations by back-propagating errors (Nature)

Q8.evidence: Backpropagation-trained networks produced breakthroughs in vision, speech, language, games and protein folding.
Q8.falsification: this pass dies if backpropagation successes are shown to be confined to one field

evaluations.bottleneck: Before stochastic gradient descent, optimizing models on large datasets was impossible or impractical because exact batch gradients required processing all data for every parameter update.

Q1.evidence: The Robbins-Monro procedure converges using noisy single-sample estimates, making iterative optimization feasible where exact gradients are unavailable or too costly.
Q1.falsification: this pass dies if exact batch optimization is shown to have been equally feasible for streaming large-scale problems in 1951
Q1.source: A Stochastic Approximation Method (Annals of Mathematical Statistics)

Q10.evidence: SGD displaced exact batch optimization as the default for training large models.
Q10.falsification: this pass dies if exact batch methods remained the default for large-model training
Q10.source: A Stochastic Approximation Method (Annals of Mathematical Statistics)

Q11.evidence: Adam, AdamW and other LLM optimizers are direct descendants that modify the SGD update rule.
Q11.falsification: this pass dies if LLM optimizers are shown to be unrelated to stochastic gradient updates
Q11.source: A Stochastic Approximation Method (Annals of Mathematical Statistics)

Q12.evidence: Large-scale model training has never returned to exact full-batch optimization since data scales grew.
Q12.falsification: this pass dies if frontier training reverts to full-batch exact gradients
Q12.source: A Stochastic Approximation Method (Annals of Mathematical Statistics)

Q2.evidence: SGD and its variants train models across vision, language, recommendation and reinforcement learning.

Q2.source: A Stochastic Approximation Method (Annals of Mathematical Statistics)

Q3.evidence: LLM training still proceeds by minibatch stochastic gradient updates; full-batch gradient descent is computationally infeasible at trillion-token scale.

Q3.source: A Stochastic Approximation Method (Annals of Mathematical Statistics)

Q4.evidence: Replacing a full dataset pass per update with a small minibatch reduces the cost of each optimization step by orders of magnitude.

Q4.source: A Stochastic Approximation Method (Annals of Mathematical Statistics)

Q7.evidence: The minibatch gradient step is the standard optimizer interface implemented by every deep learning framework.
Q7.falsification: this pass dies if frameworks are shown not to be organized around minibatch gradient steps
Q7.source: A Stochastic Approximation Method (Annals of Mathematical Statistics)

Q8.evidence: Stochastic approximation is used in statistics, control, finance and machine learning, far beyond its original setting.
Q8.falsification: this pass dies if stochastic approximation is shown to have remained a statistics curiosity
Q8.source: A Stochastic Approximation Method (Annals of Mathematical Statistics)

evaluations.bottleneck: Before Adam optimizer, training deep networks was impractical at scale because SGD required extensive per-problem learning-rate tuning and handled sparse gradients poorly.

Q7.falsification: this pass dies if frameworks are shown not to have adopted Adam as a standard default

evaluations.bottleneck: Before scaling laws for neural language models, planning large training runs was impossible or impractical because no one knew how loss would respond to more model, data and compute.

Q5.source: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models

Q1.evidence: AlexNet cut ImageNet top-5 error to 15.3 percent versus 26.2 percent for the runner-up, a gap hand-engineered methods had not approached.
Q1.falsification: this pass dies if the 2012 ImageNet margin is shown to be small or achieved by a non-neural method
Q1.source: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks

Q10.evidence: After 2012, learned convolutional features displaced hand-engineered SIFT-style features as the computer vision default.
Q10.falsification: this pass dies if hand-engineered features remained the vision default after 2014
Q10.source: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks

Q11.evidence: AlexNet is the recognized ignition point of the deep learning era from which Transformer and LLM work followed.
Q11.falsification: this pass dies if the deep learning era is shown to have begun independently of the 2012 result
Q11.source: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks

Q12.evidence: Computer vision never returned to hand-engineered features as its leading approach after AlexNet.
Q12.falsification: this pass dies if hand-engineered features regain the lead in vision benchmarks
Q12.source: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks

Q2.evidence: AlexNet's win triggered deep learning adoption across speech, translation, drug discovery and game playing within five years.
Q2.falsification: this pass dies if deep learning adoption after 2012 is shown to be unrelated to the ImageNet result
Q2.source: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks

Q8.evidence: GPU-trained deep networks modeled on AlexNet produced breakthroughs in speech recognition and machine translation by 2016.
Q8.falsification: this pass dies if post-AlexNet deep learning is shown to have stayed within image classification
Q8.source: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks

evaluations.bottleneck: Before ImageNet dataset, training and comparing data-hungry perception models was impossible or impractical because available labeled image sets were too small and had no common benchmark.

Q2.evidence: ImageNet's 14 million labeled images enabled training data-hungry models and spawned benchmarks and challenges across vision subfields.
Q2.falsification: this pass dies if large-scale vision progress is shown to have proceeded equally on pre-2009 small datasets
Q2.source: ImageNet: A Large-Scale Hierarchical Image Database

Q5.evidence: The ImageNet challenge gave perception a single public error-rate metric on which competing methods could be ranked annually.
Q5.falsification: this pass dies if ImageNet is shown not to have provided a common comparative metric
Q5.source: ImageNet: A Large-Scale Hierarchical Image Database

Q7.evidence: ImageNet's category structure and train-test protocol became the standard benchmark interface for vision research.
Q7.falsification: this pass dies if vision research is shown not to have standardized on ImageNet protocols
Q7.source: ImageNet: A Large-Scale Hierarchical Image Database

Q8.evidence: ImageNet pre-training transferred to medical imaging, robotics and remote sensing far outside its original object categories.
Q8.falsification: this pass dies if ImageNet pre-training is shown not to transfer outside object recognition
Q8.source: ImageNet: A Large-Scale Hierarchical Image Database

evaluations.bottleneck: Before CUDA, using GPU parallelism for general computation was impossible or impractical because graphics hardware could only be programmed through graphics APIs not designed for it.

Q1.evidence: CUDA gave general-purpose code direct access to GPU parallel cores, making GPU matrix computation practical for non-graphics programmers.
Q1.falsification: this pass dies if general-purpose GPU computing is shown to have been equally accessible through graphics APIs before 2007

Q10.evidence: GPUs displaced CPUs as the default compute for training neural networks after CUDA matured.
Q10.falsification: this pass dies if CPUs remained the default training hardware after 2012

Q11.evidence: Every stage of the agent lineage from AlexNet to GPT training ran on CUDA-programmed NVIDIA hardware.
Q11.falsification: this pass dies if the main lineage systems are shown to have trained primarily on other platforms

Q12.evidence: The AI field's software and hardware investment is now locked into the CUDA ecosystem, with alternatives still chasing compatibility.
Q12.falsification: this pass dies if the field migrates wholesale off the CUDA ecosystem

Q2.evidence: CUDA enabled GPU acceleration across deep learning, molecular dynamics, finance and scientific simulation.
Q2.falsification: this pass dies if CUDA use is shown to be confined to deep learning
Q2.source: CUDA (Wikipedia)

Q3.evidence: Frontier LLM training runs execute overwhelmingly on NVIDIA GPUs programmed through the CUDA ecosystem.
Q3.falsification: this pass dies if frontier LLM training is shown to run mainly on non-CUDA hardware at comparable scale

Q4.evidence: GPU training reduced deep network training times from weeks on CPUs to days, as first demonstrated at scale by AlexNet's two-GPU training.
Q4.falsification: this pass dies if GPU training is shown to offer no large speedup over CPU training for deep networks

Q7.evidence: CUDA became the standard programming interface that frameworks such as PyTorch target so users need not write GPU kernels themselves.
Q7.falsification: this pass dies if deep learning frameworks are shown not to build on CUDA
Q7.source: CUDA (Wikipedia)

Q8.evidence: CUDA-based computing is standard in physics simulation, genomics and quantitative finance as well as AI.
Q8.falsification: this pass dies if CUDA is shown to have no significant use outside AI

Q9.evidence: Orders-of-magnitude faster training let researchers run many more architecture and hyperparameter experiments per month.
Q9.falsification: this pass dies if experiment throughput in deep learning is shown not to have risen with GPU adoption

evaluations.bottleneck: Before Perceptron, a machine learning a classifier from examples was impossible or impractical because computing machines were programmed with fixed rules rather than adjusted weights.

Before Turing's learning machine proposal, conceiving intelligence as trained rather than programmed was impossible or impractical because machines were understood only as executing hand-written rules.
Before information theory (Shannon), quantifying information and communication limits was impossible or impractical because there was no mathematical measure of information content.

Q11.evidence: Perplexity and cross-entropy, the central metrics of the LLM lineage, are direct Shannon quantities.
Q11.falsification: this pass dies if LLM evaluation is shown not to use entropy-derived metrics

Q12.evidence: No alternative framework has displaced entropy as the measure of information in any technical field since 1948.
Q12.falsification: this pass dies if a non-Shannon measure becomes the standard for information content

Q2.evidence: Information theory founded digital communication, data compression, error-correcting codes and statistical language modeling.
Q2.falsification: this pass dies if those fields are shown to rest on foundations independent of Shannon's theory
Q2.source: A Mathematical Theory of Communication

Q3.evidence: Language model training loss is cross-entropy, a quantity defined directly in Shannon's entropy framework.
Q3.falsification: this pass dies if language modeling loss is shown to be definable without entropy concepts

Q5.evidence: Shannon entropy gave the first rigorous numerical measure of the information content of a source.
Q5.falsification: this pass dies if an earlier rigorous measure of information content is shown to predate 1948

Q6.evidence: Entropy and channel capacity provided the explanatory model used to design codes and, later, to interpret perplexity in language models.
Q6.falsification: this pass dies if code and language model design are shown to make no use of entropy or capacity concepts

Q7.evidence: Bits, entropy and channel capacity became the shared standard vocabulary across communications, computing and machine learning.
Q7.falsification: this pass dies if those fields are shown not to share Shannon's quantities as standard terms
Q7.source: A Mathematical Theory of Communication

Q8.evidence: Information theory is applied in physics, biology, economics and neuroscience as well as communications.
Q8.falsification: this pass dies if information theory is shown to be used only in communications engineering

evaluations.bottleneck: Before cross-entropy loss, scoring a predicted distribution against reality was impossible or impractical because there was no principled loss measuring distributional mismatch for training classifiers.

Q10.evidence: Cross-entropy displaced error-rate and squared-error objectives as the default for probabilistic classification.
Q10.falsification: this pass dies if squared error remained the default classification loss in neural networks

Q11.evidence: The scaling laws and training curves of the LLM lineage are plotted in cross-entropy loss.
Q11.falsification: this pass dies if LLM training progress is shown to be tracked in a different primary quantity

Q12.evidence: Frontier language models are still trained by minimizing cross-entropy more than seventy years after its derivation.
Q12.falsification: this pass dies if frontier language model training abandons cross-entropy

Q2.evidence: Cross-entropy is the training objective for classifiers, language models and many structured prediction systems across machine learning.
Q2.falsification: this pass dies if major classifier and language model families are shown to train on unrelated objectives
Q2.source: Entropy (information theory) (Wikipedia)

Q3.evidence: Next-token pre-training of every GPT-class model is defined as minimizing cross-entropy loss.
Q3.falsification: this pass dies if GPT-class pre-training is shown to use a different primary objective

Q5.evidence: Cross-entropy turns model quality into a single measurable number, reported as perplexity for language models.
Q5.falsification: this pass dies if cross-entropy values are shown not to track language model quality

Q6.evidence: Cross-entropy interprets training as reducing the model's surprise, giving designers a principled account of what optimization improves.
Q6.falsification: this pass dies if the surprise interpretation is shown to be mathematically incorrect

Q7.evidence: Cross-entropy is the standard loss function exposed by every machine learning framework for classification and language modeling.
Q7.falsification: this pass dies if frameworks are shown not to provide cross-entropy as a standard loss
Q7.source: Entropy (information theory) (Wikipedia)

Q8.evidence: Cross-entropy loss is used in speech recognition, machine translation, recommendation and medical diagnosis models.
Q8.falsification: this pass dies if cross-entropy use is shown to be confined to language modeling

evaluations.bottleneck: Before maximum likelihood estimation, fitting statistical models to data was impossible or impractical as a general method because estimation relied on ad hoc moment matching per problem.

Q11.evidence: Next-token training is maximum likelihood estimation applied to text sequences, placing MLE in the direct lineage of LLM cores.
Q11.falsification: this pass dies if next-token training is shown not to maximize the likelihood of training text

Q12.evidence: Likelihood-based fitting remains a default estimation principle a century after Fisher's formulation.
Q12.falsification: this pass dies if likelihood fitting is abandoned as a default across statistics and machine learning

Q2.evidence: Maximum likelihood provides one estimation principle used for regression, mixture models, hidden Markov models and language models.
Q2.falsification: this pass dies if those model families are shown not to be fitted by likelihood maximization
Q2.source: Maximum likelihood estimation (Wikipedia)

Q6.evidence: Fisher's likelihood framework supplied the explanatory model of estimation as choosing parameters that make observed data most probable, with known asymptotic properties.
Q6.falsification: this pass dies if likelihood theory is shown not to yield the claimed estimation properties

Q7.evidence: Log-likelihood is the standard objective interface implemented across statistical software and machine learning frameworks.
Q7.falsification: this pass dies if statistical software is shown not to standardize on likelihood objectives
Q7.source: Maximum likelihood estimation (Wikipedia)

Q8.evidence: Maximum likelihood is routine in genetics, econometrics, epidemiology and physics as well as machine learning.
Q8.falsification: this pass dies if maximum likelihood is shown to be used only within statistics

evaluations.bottleneck: Before Bayesian probability (Bayes' theorem), updating beliefs from evidence was impossible or impractical as a formal procedure because probability was not defined for hypotheses themselves.

Q2.evidence: Bayes' theorem underpins methods used in medicine, spam filtering, robotics state estimation and scientific inference.
Q2.falsification: this pass dies if those fields are shown not to use Bayesian updating
Q2.source: An Essay towards solving a Problem in the Doctrine of Chances

Q6.evidence: Bayes' theorem gives the canonical explanatory model of learning as prior belief revised by likelihood of evidence.
Q6.falsification: this pass dies if the prior-times-likelihood formulation is shown not to describe Bayesian inference
Q6.source: An Essay towards solving a Problem in the Doctrine of Chances

Q8.evidence: Bayesian methods are standard in clinical trials, astrophysics, ecology and law as well as machine learning.
Q8.falsification: this pass dies if Bayesian methods are shown to be confined to machine learning
Q8.source: An Essay towards solving a Problem in the Doctrine of Chances
